003:scene001 clarifies that Ritsu's planting is deliveries, not a body burial. She names sculpture and trading as hobby/skill and sculpture as major. Her offering Teacher clothes after a reported embarrassing news story is a wanted helpful gesture, politely declined, not completed dressing or verified whole earlier history. Delivery points show a student happily retrieving desired fried chicken and another receiving banned paint to finish work. The painting ban is explained through alleged insecticide danger; narrator's impression that inspected goods were less alarming than imagined does not prove all goods harmless. Other routes exist by club report, but the observed few are the actual scope.

003:scene004 turns planning into a literary work: Fuyu and Ritsu praise Miyo's routes and encounter scripts. Their praise matters, but Miyo says it is embarrassing and initially refuses the next large commission. Fuyu introduces the rare キューティーベリー87, which Miyo has long wanted, then the prospect of enough pay to buy several. Its description includes an attached directional antipersonnel mine, a counterpoint to simplistic harmless collecting and Fuyu's own cool catapult. Miyo's affection for a commercially rejected device and aesthetic language are intrinsic desires, not pathology, nor automatically superior judgment. The temptation wins permission to hear the commission, not immediate unconditional acceptance.

004 flashes back to the preceding day. Fuyu explicitly refuses a proposed painting removal as theft and jokingly rejects nonexistent robbery/thief clubs, then hears the client's claimed past forgery, remorse and wish to substitute a true painting. She suggests truthful disclosure to the foundation and asks how the client proves which painting is genuine (scene002:u0053–0076). Technical/commercial confidence coexists with moral and attribution questions. The client's offer to let them destroy or retain the removed work without public display persuades, but it is a claim offered as evidence, not independent authentication. His disdain for ignorant audiences and wish to erase his record qualify the remorse story.

Fuyu has received the purported genuine painting but has not independently accepted the commission; she says she will return it if Miyo refuses. Ritsu calls it pretty, Miyo is excited to see it close and the projected payment would fund wanted fine marble as well as the typewriter. Teacher says monitoring and trust in students make the job acceptable, while Miyo maintains it is money-driven theft. She agrees with an inward resolution that it will be her last job (u0123–0136). Teacher's reassurance is part of the pressure/confidence structure, not the analyst's certification of legality or truth.

3. Affection, fatigue and an inadequate first plot
005:scene001 Ritsu's hammer is actually preparation for sculpture, not Fuyu's joke about striking Miyo awake. Miyo spent the night designing the operation, dislikes its direction rather than all her writing, and is warmed by Ritsu's favorite-author declaration. Fuyu asks for comparable affection and is ignored. These unequal responses are not unanimous peer appreciation or completed intimacy. Miyo proposes targeting storage before exhibition; she refuses smashing the wall, partly because repair was not funded. Her expertise is printed planning, not faultless forecasting.

Hiromi in scene002 is a literature peer and Dormitory Guard deputy. Both have signs/reports of fatigue. Guarding the exhibition has crowded out smuggling enforcement. She feels able to relax with Miyo because she believes her uninvolved; Miyo's inward apology preserves the compromised trust, without a confession or later repaired friendship being printed. Miyo notices Hiromi's subdued voice and asks; Hiromi shares a thief's warning letter. That attentiveness has ordinary relational value even as the secret activity frustrates Hiromi's work.

006 distinguishes Miyo's copied text from the original kept by guards. The warning is no longer treated as confidential because no one can decipher it, per Miyo's report. Stronger security defeats her first all-night plan and requires rewriting. In the library Miyo helps Eri with dropped books, asks painting questions and uses Eri's proposed lapis/ultramarine link to redirect research toward pigments. Eri explicitly denies general gem expertise, grounding it in her painting studies. Occult book titles supply a reading repertoire, not successful magic or a verified metaphysics. All etymology/material-history explanations remain the characters' source-local reasoning; no external scientific verification is claimed.

007 completes the collaborative interpretation: Miyo proposes costly blue/purple pigments and royal exclusivity, Ritsu recognizes the title's relevant painting, Fuyu contributes media-art/photography knowledge and distinguishes sunrise from sunset; Ritsu supplies the closing-doors clue. The interpretation concludes おそらく, and the actual later evening appearance supports the local fit. Not all textual reasoning becomes universally true art history. Teacher brings cake, Ritsu actually praises/eats it, and Fuyu's plan to turn Teacher into an import business is explicitly refused. Welcome food and a commercial boundary coexist.

Miyo reframes the job so the thief removes the stored purported forgery while the club inserts the supposedly true work. She resents praise for criminal talent and says she wanted romance novels; when Teacher wants to read one she explicitly refuses (u0063–0074). Respect her desired genre and refusal. She elects to support the thief, trusting a report that stolen works never return to circulation; that mistaken authentication premise and strategic hope must reach the later outcome.
